attributes.cardDescription: A physical package — separate from the order because one order can become two packages and two orders can become one.
attributes.readMe:
## Shipment (Sh)

Kept separate from the order on purpose. One order becomes two shipments when stock sits in two warehouses; two orders become one when a customer buys twice in a morning. Neither is expressible if a shipment is a set of fields on the order.

**Everything from the carrier is snapshotted, not read through the link.** Carrier name, service name, tracking URL pattern, dimensional divisor and quoted cost are stamped onto the shipment when the label is created. A carrier renaming a service two years from now must not rewrite what happened to a package that has already arrived.

`isLate` is derived from the promise and the actual, not stored — both halves are already on the card, so a stored flag would only be a third thing to keep in step. `shippingMargin` is computed because losing money on the shipping line is the number worth surfacing.

`TrackingEventField` (also exported here) is one carrier scan, stored verbatim. The sequence is what a customer-service conversation is actually about, so it is not collapsed into the status.

The isolated view mounts `ShipmentTracker` rather than drawing a second timeline.

### Example

Six shipments: one delivered on time, one delivered late, one out for delivery, one in transit, one dropship in exception (`SHP-2026-0142`), and one whose volumetric weight cost more than the customer paid.

### Non-goals

No label generation. `labelUrl` is stored and linked, but nothing renders a PDF or ZPL — a label renderer is a separate block with its own owner.
